title: Qwen4 Max Preview: Benchmarks, Cost and Speed
summary: Qwen4 Max just launched; nobody has tested it on real work yet. See how it integrates into automation platforms and what early tests should focus on.
body_markdown:
## What Activepieces lets you do with a new model like Qwen4 Max


A new release should be one step you swap while the other connections stay as you built them.


### Your own key, your own model choice


**Activepieces doesn't tie you to one model** , and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production: you choose the model, and you can change it in one step without rebuilding the flow around it.


Nothing on the maker's page tells you whether Qwen4 Max is available through your provider yet, so confirm that before you plan the test.


Swapping the model changes one step and leaves the rest of the flow as it was.


Bring-your-own-key starts on the Plus plan at $20 a month, where every AI step is 1 credit and the model cost lands on your own provider bill; without your own key, the same step costs 2, 10 or 20 credits for a fast, smart or frontier model, at $0.007 a credit over the 10,000 included each month.


Do not assume Qwen4 Max is already a listed option: it is a day old, and whether your provider offers it is something you confirm, not something to take on trust.


Treat Qwen4 Max as something you try once your provider offers it and then confirm works. The maker's page and your own test are the whole record of what it can do.


### Connecting it in a workflow today


Pick one workflow your team already runs, one with a clear before and after, such as triaging inbound email. Keep the current model in place and add a second AI step beside it for the model you want to test.


In the builder, the test flow shows the shape. A schedule trigger feeds Google Sheets rows through a loop, a date helper and an HTTP request into two AI steps, then a router splits the results into branches and Gmail sends the outcome.


To compare, you need two AI steps in one flow. Point one at the model you use now and the other at Qwen4 Max, with the same prompt and the same input rows.


Then your team reads both outputs side by side in the sheet, not in a launch headline.
